body:
## Summary

#239 (the fix for #238) lowers the sampler's rate to one round every 5 s and resolves `CgroupnsMode` once. When the task container's cgroup cannot be read where `$` runs, which is the usual case with a mounted `docker.sock`, every round still starts a **new `docker exec`** into the task container plus a `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}'`. The cost per sample stays the same; only the rate drops. One long-lived exec per sampler would remove almost all of the remaining per-round work and keep the same samples.

## Setup where this happens

link-assistant/hive-mind runs `$` inside its own container. That container mounts the host's `/var/run/docker.sock` and has its own PID and cgroup namespaces. Task containers are siblings on the host daemon. Checked on the host:

- `/proc/<task .State.Pid>` is not visible from where `$` runs (the PID belongs to another PID namespace).
- `/sys/fs/cgroup` there shows only the hive-mind container's own cgroup (`/proc/self/cgroup` is `0::/`), and `system.slice/` does not exist.
- So `__start_command_cgroup_dir` returns nothing, the task containers have `CgroupnsMode=private`, and every round takes the `docker exec … sh -c '<functions>; __start_command_cgroup_read /sys/fs/cgroup'` path.

## Measured (start-command 0.37.8, 1 s interval, 3 tasks, 6-CPU host, 20 s window)

| Per task | Rate |
|---|---|
| sampler rounds | 36/min |
| `docker exec` into the task container | 15/min |
| `runc` started by that container's shim | 21/min |
| `docker inspect -f {{.State.Running}}` | 15–24/min |
| `docker inspect -f {{.HostConfig.CgroupnsMode}}` (fixed by #239) | 18–27/min |
| CPU of the sampler loop and its children | 0.25–0.30 cores |

containerd and the shims used 0.22 cores and dockerd 0.10 cores for the 3 tasks together. That is shared with other Docker clients on the host, so not all of it is the sampler.

With `main` (calculated, not measured): about 12 `docker exec` and 12 `docker inspect` per minute per task. Each exec costs a Docker API call, a `runc` exec in the shim, and about 7 short processes inside the task container (`sh`, three `cat`, two `sed` pipelines). These are counted against the task's own CPU limit.

## Suggested changes (no behaviour change for callers)

1. **One long-lived exec per sampler in the fallback path.** Start `docker exec <name> sh -c 'while :; do <read memory.events / memory.max / memory.peak>; echo; sleep N; done'` once and read one line per interval from its stdout into the same sample file.
   - Shell builtins (`read` from `memory.events`) avoid the per-round `cat`/`sed` processes inside the container.
   - The exec ends when the container stops, so it also replaces the per-round liveness probe.
   - If the long-lived exec cannot start (no `sh` in the image, exec refused), fall back to today's per-round exec.
2. **Drop or thin out the per-round `docker inspect -f {{.State.Running}}`.** The completion watcher already stops the sampler after `docker wait` (as the comment in `cgroup-memory.js` says). If it stays as a safety net, every Nth round is enough.
3. **Allow turning sampling off.** For example `START_COMMAND_CGROUP_SAMPLE_INTERVAL_SECONDS=off`, for callers that do not need OOM evidence. Today `0` and invalid values fall back to the default, so a new explicit value does not change existing behaviour.

The #209 trade-off (an OOM kill after the last sample) is unaffected: a streaming exec keeps the same interval, or allows a shorter one at the same cost.

Related: #238, #239, #240 (the release that would ship #239 is skipped), link-assistant/hive-mind#3614.
title: Docker cgroup sampler: with a mounted docker.sock every round still starts a new docker exec and docker inspect (use one long-lived exec)
